title: Module builder: author a form with sample ghost pre-fill + draft completeness check
walkthrough:
You start on "Your product dossiers", under a top bar branded "ANDS Studio" with chips for "Help", "Portfolio", "Registry", "Correspondence" and "Guided journey →". Each dossier is a tile showing its ID, product name, a progress bar, and a chip reading either "Ready to file" or a count like "2/5 modules". Clicking a tile opens the dossier at Module 1. (Creating a new one requires a Dossier ID in a specific format — "Dossier ID must be one letter + 6–7 digits (e.g. e123456)" — or you click "No ID yet? Start with a placeholder →".)

Inside, the top bar shows module tabs M1–M5 with status glyphs, plus "Application Viewer", "Audit", "Portfolio" and "Journey" chips. The workspace is three columns: a left section tree; a center panel; and a right rail. The tree now opens with a persistent legend mapping the glyphs — ○ Not started, ◐ In progress, ✓ Complete, ⊘ N/A — above the sections, each of which carries its own glyph, a "req"/"opt" badge, an optional "✦AI" badge, and a collapsed "Not required for this generic (N)" list. The right rail shows module progress ("3/7 required sections complete") and readiness flags "Documents", "Fee", "Valid eCTD"; if any worked-example values remain it shows a red "N sample/AI draft value(s) remain — each must be reviewed and confirmed as your own content before this submission can be filed or exported."

Selecting a section shows an eyebrow line ("Module 1 · Section 1.2.5 · required"), the title, its purpose, and a teach box "What Health Canada needs here" with format notes and a "Health Canada guidance ↗" link. A tab bar offers "⬆ Upload", "✦ Author in-app", and "⊘ Mark N/A". Regulatory field labels carry glossary tooltips.

Choosing "✦ Author in-app" opens a form (for AI-eligible sections, a toggle "💬 Draft with AI" / "✦ Fill the form" appears first). A note explains your dossier's known facts are pre-filled, and fields marked "sample" show a "ghost example" — placeholder text you must replace — that is never saved as your content. Sample fields carry a "sample — replace" tag and show the example only as greyed "e.g. …" placeholder text. Fields carry regulatory labels like "Drug product", "Canadian Reference Product (brand)", "s.5 statement (per patent)" and "AUC 90% CI". You edit them, then click "Author {section title} →" (it reads "Authoring…" while busy), or run a check first via the ghost button "Review vs Health Canada", which returns "Health Canada review:" plus "no blocking content gaps." or a count like "2 to fix, 1 to check." with per-finding suggested edits and "HC guidance ↗" links.

If a section still holds an unedited worked example, its saved-document card shows a persistent, sighted banner: "⚠ Not yet filable — review required. This section still shows worked-example (sample) values." It will not count as complete and cannot be exported until you replace every example value and re-author; the example is detected server-side, so it clears automatically once no example values remain (there is nothing to "confirm" while it is still in place). AI-assisted drafts instead carry a confirm button, "I have reviewed this AI draft — it is my content". The document lists with filename, size, "fingerprint md5 ……", a provenance chip ("authored in-app", "uploaded", "AI draft — review & confirm", etc.), and a "Download" link.

The right rail also carries a "Draft completeness check" card. It states in plain terms that it "checks presence and format only, not scientific adequacy or full eCTD technical validation. Run Health Canada's eValidator before you transmit." When criteria are present it names a versioned structural profile with a disclaimer and a "What this does / does NOT check" expander listing checked and not-checked items. Findings carry rule ids (CA-E-…/CA-W-…). A footer states this is "not a Health Canada review and not full eCTD technical validation. Where a checksum is shown it is document control (md5), not validation." Buttons run a technical check (PDF header/encryption) and download the report (CSV/JSON). On Module 1 a separate "Product Monograph (1.3.1)" card shows bilingual status chips ("✓/○ English", "✓/○ French") with a "Blocked"/"Bilingual complete" state, and an "XML Product Monograph" affordance to paste and "Validate XML PM" against the schema/stylesheet rules, noting Health Canada "is phasing in a mandatory structured XML Product Monograph."
